label: Iterative Estimation Methods
notes: This appendix spans printed pages 597 through 627 and treats nonlinear estimation as repeated local linearization. We minimize geometric reprojection error rather than an algebraic surrogate, so each residual carries pixel units. The thread runs from Newton through Gauss-Newton and Levenberg-Marquardt to sparse bundle adjustment.

label: The Nonlinear Least-Squares Problem
notes: State the target precisely: find parameters that minimize the squared norm of a vector of residuals measuring geometric error. The cost surface is nonlinear and non-convex, so we cannot solve in one shot. Stress that geometric error in image units is the quantity we actually care about.

label: Newton's Method
notes: Newton uses the full Hessian, so it needs second derivatives of every residual. Near a minimum it converges quadratically, but the Hessian is expensive and can be indefinite far from the solution, sending steps uphill. This motivates the cheaper Gauss-Newton approximation that follows.

label: Gauss-Newton
notes: Gauss-Newton drops the second-derivative term and approximates the Hessian by J-transpose-J. The step solves the normal equations built from the Jacobian alone. It is fast and accurate near the solution where residuals are small, but it offers no safeguard when the linear model is a poor fit far away.

label: Gradient Descent and the Two Regimes
notes: Gradient descent moves along the negative gradient and is robust but slow, crawling through narrow valleys. Gauss-Newton is fast but reckless. Levenberg-Marquardt blends the two so the solver can be cautious when far out and aggressive when close, choosing automatically rather than by hand.

label: Levenberg-Marquardt
notes: Levenberg-Marquardt augments the diagonal of the normal matrix with a damping term lambda. Small lambda recovers Gauss-Newton; large lambda yields a short gradient-descent step. After each trial the step is accepted or rejected and lambda is adapted from the trust ratio, the agreement between predicted and actual reduction.

label: Damping as a Trust Region
notes: Reframe damping geometrically: increasing lambda shrinks the region in which we trust the local quadratic model, so the step gets shorter and bends toward steepest descent. The notebook confirms step norms fall monotonically as lambda grows while predicted reductions stay positive, exactly the trust-region picture.

label: Convergence Diagnostics
notes: A final parameter vector is not evidence. We audit four traces together: accepted objective, damping lambda, the trust ratio comparing actual to predicted reduction, and pixel residual statistics. Accepted objectives are monotone non-increasing, and the median pixel error falls below one pixel by the end.

label: Parametrization and the Manifold
notes: Many vision quantities live on manifolds, not flat vector spaces. Over-parametrization with a constraint or a redundant rotation representation distorts the update. We prefer a minimal local parametrization and apply the increment on the manifold so each step respects the geometry of the unknown.

label: Robust Cost and Influence
notes: Outliers wreck a pure least-squares fit. A robust cost is rewritten as a weighted residual norm with an attenuation factor, downweighting large residuals through iteratively reweighted solves. The notebook shows Cauchy attenuation cutting outlier influence while keeping the bad points visible in the diagnostic, not deleted.

label: Sparse Bundle Adjustment
notes: In bundle adjustment the unknowns split into camera blocks and point blocks, and one observation touches exactly one camera and one point. The normal matrix gains a block arrowhead structure. Exploiting this sparsity is what makes adjusting thousands of cameras and points computationally tractable at all.

label: The Schur Complement Reduction
notes: Eliminate the point blocks first. The Schur complement folds point information into a much smaller reduced camera system, which we solve, then back-substitute for the points. The notebook verifies the Schur camera and point steps match the dense solve to machine precision: same step, cheaper route.

label: Synthesis and Takeaways
notes: Tie the appendix together: iterative estimation is repeated local linearization plus disciplined step acceptance. Levenberg-Marquardt interpolates cautious descent and fast Gauss-Newton. Robust costs change influence, not existence. Schur structure is the computational reason large multiple-view optimizations are solvable. Always keep the starting estimate and residual units in view.
